title: vllm-project/semantic-router — A programmable Mixture-of-Models router for heterogeneous LLM inference
content:
Make Your Mixture-of-Models Programmable.
Documentation | Playground | Blog | Publications | Hugging Face | Slack
vLLM Semantic Router is a programmable routing layer for building Mixture-of-Models systems across heterogeneous LLM infrastructure. It evaluates request signals, user preferences, and application policies to select—or compose—the right model path for each request.
Use it to improve quality, cost, latency, privacy, and safety without hard-coding routing logic into applications.
curl -fsSL https://vllm-sr.ai/install.sh | bash
For platform notes, detailed setup options, and troubleshooting, see the Installation Guide.

report.summary: vLLM Semantic Router is a programmable routing layer that dynamically selects or composes AI models for optimized quality, cost, and latency.
report.background: As organizations deploy multiple LLMs across cloud, on-prem, and edge infrastructure, a single model rarely fits every request. Latency, cost, privacy, accuracy, and safety requirements vary by task, user, and context. The vLLM project, already a leading open-source inference engine, launched Semantic Router in late 2025 to address this fragmentation. The tool evaluates request signals, user preferences, and application policies to route each query to the most suitable model or combine multiple models in a Mixture-of-Models setup. It has evolved rapidly through multiple releases—Iris, Athena, and Themis—adding stateful production routing, semantic caching, hallucination detection, and LoRA support. Partnerships with AMD and the vLLM Production Stack team signal enterprise traction. By making routing programmable, it removes hard-coded model selection logic from applications, enabling dynamic, policy-driven inference at scale.
key_points: Semantic Router decouples model choice from application code: Developers no longer hard-code which LLM handles a request. Instead, the router evaluates signals like user preference, task type, cost constraints, or privacy requirements, then selects or composes the optimal model path per request.

It supports Mixture-of-Models by composition, not just selection: Beyond choosing one model, the router can fuse outputs from multiple models or route to specialized micro-agents. This lets teams combine frontier models with smaller, cheaper models to balance quality and cost without rewriting application logic.

Production features have matured through stable releases: The v0.3 Themis release moved from simple signal routing to stateful production routing. The roadmap includes semantic caching and real-time hallucination detection, which are critical for real-world reliability and operational efficiency.

The project is backed by major ecosystem players and open collaboration: AMD provides GPU resources and ROCm software for training router models and building a playground. Regular community meetings and a Slack channel invite contributors, positioning the project as a neutral, community-driven standard rather than a vendor lock-in.

It addresses a key industry pain point: heterogeneous LLM infrastructure. Enterprises rarely standardize on one model. Semantic Router creates a control plane across vLLM and other backends, enabling teams to enforce policies like data privacy (e.g., routing sensitive requests to on-prem models) or latency budgets automatically.
report.impact: For the AI industry, Semantic Router represents a shift from model-centric development to workload-centric orchestration. It makes Mixture-of-Models practical, allowing companies to use frontier models only when needed, cutting inference costs and latency. Developers benefit from a clean abstraction: they can write routing policies declaratively and iterate without touching application code. Regular users see faster, cheaper, and safer AI interactions, as requests are sent to the model best suited for the task—such as a small local model for simple queries or a larger model for complex reasoning. Privacy-sensitive use cases gain a straightforward way to enforce data residency rules. By integrating with vLLM's production stack, the project could become the standard routing layer for self-hosted and hybrid LLM deployments, reducing dependence on single-vendor APIs.
report.tools: To explore semantic routing, start with vLLM Semantic Router itself (github.com/vllm-project/semantic-router), which includes documentation, a playground, and a one-line installer. Related open-source projects include vLLM for high-throughput inference, LlamaIndex or Haystack for building LLM pipelines with routing abstractions, and LiteLLM for unified model gateway features. For caching and optimization, watch vLLM's semantic cache integrations and tools like GPTCache. The project's blog and publications page offers deep dives into signal-driven routing and Mixture-of-Models architecture.
